cues.text: Hi, Professor Timmons? Do you have a few minutes? I was hoping to talk about what I missed on Thursday.
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: Hello, come in. Sure, sit down. Could you tell me your name please?
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Margaret, sir. Margaret Parkinson. I apologize for missing your class but I had to go to the hospital.
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: I’m sorry to hear that! Everything is OK now though, I hope?
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Yes, thanks.
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: Glad to hear it. So on Thursday I outlined the research project that will account for 30% of your grade. All students will be divided into groups and will give a well-researched presentation to the class covering a specific topic relevant to student life.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Oh, that sounds interesting - can we choose just any topic that pertains to life as a student, like how to start your own student organization?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: Well, though I’m sure that would be an informative presentation, I have already chosen a list of topics which I will assign. As an example, I assigned one group the topic of student loans. They are to research not just the prevalence of students who have loans to pay for their tuition but information as to how best to manage these loans and possible scholarships that could alleviate some of the financial burden.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: That one sounds particularly interesting to me - could I request that topic? I could easily find out a lot about it by stopping by the Finance Office on my way to class.
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: Unfortunately, that one is already taken by another group. I have, however, assigned you to a group and given you all one of two choices.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Oh, I see. What are the choices?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: The first is discussing smoking. Trends in the number of student smokers compared with the general population, popular reasons students take up smoking, and more healthy alternatives to smoking.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Hm, that one could be interesting. I’m not a smoker myself, but will see what my group thinks. If we did choose this topic, we would rather not put our fellow students on the spot to interview them - Where else could we gather information?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: How about where the cigarettes are sold?
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Oh, that’s a great idea. I could interview the manager of a supermarket and find out the average age of people buying cigarettes, or how much they buy, that sort of thing?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: Precisely.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Okay, I’ll keep that in mind. And what was the other topic?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: The other topic is the practice of natural medicine. It sounds far more specific than the others, but it is more an exercise of outlining a career path. If your group chooses this, you would cover the specifics of becoming a Doctor of Natural Medicine, how to become licensed to practice natural medicine, what the career outlook is, etc. you could find much of the information you need on this in the Careers Office.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Wow, That would be really helpful not just in learning about natural medicine, but in how to approach researching any career path.
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: That’s the idea. I want groups to really think outside the box to find information on their topics. They should interview multiple sources.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Okay, now I think I have the general idea.
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: When is the presentation due?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: I expect each group to send me an email attachment of the plan ahead of time - by October 10th - so that I can ensure that you are on the right track.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Oh, that’s actually really reassuring. I would hate to spend so much time on a presentation only to find we had taken it in the wrong direction! So when is the presentation?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: I let groups choose from the list of time slots I have between November 1st and November 5th.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Okay, how about the 3rd? I’ll have to check with my group, of course, but maybe we could write a tentative time?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: Sure, let me take a look. I’m actually booked completely through the 3rd and 4th now. How about sometime in the afternoon of the 5th?
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Great! How about 2 o’clock?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: No problem. I’ll pencil your group in.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Okay, thanks. And to clarify, what exactly is due in the first phase?
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: Before the October deadline, I want your group to have compiled resources and then to provide some initial data analysis to support your claims.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Okay, so data analysis is due the 10th of October, and then the um, the -
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: - Presentation? Yes. The final phase is simply giving the presentation on the 5th of November.
cues.speaker: Professor

cues.text: Alright, I think I have all the information I need. Thanks!
cues.speaker: Student

cues.text: You’re welcome. See you in class tomorrow.
cues.speaker: Professor
